html:
Operation Blue Star was the Indian army's assault on the Golden Temple at Amritsar in June 1984, to remove armed Sikh militants. It set off the worst year in India since Partition.

In the early 1980s a preacher, Jarnail Singh Bhindranwale, gathered armed followers in Punjab. Some Sikhs wanted more power for the state; a few wanted a separate country, Khalistan. Killings of Hindus and of Sikh opponents mounted. Bhindranwale moved into the temple complex, the holiest place of the Sikhs, and fortified it.

Indira Gandhi sent in the army. The main attack came on the night of 5 June, a holy day when the complex was full of pilgrims. The defenders were well armed, and the army brought in tanks. The government counted 83 soldiers and 493 others dead; other counts are much higher. The Akal Takht, the seat of Sikh authority, was left in ruins.

Sikhs everywhere were shocked. On 31 October 1984 two of the prime minister's Sikh bodyguards shot her dead in her garden. Over the next three days mobs, some led by Congress politicians, killed about 3,000 Sikhs in Delhi and other cities. Few were ever punished.

An armed revolt in Punjab went on for a decade and cost some 20,000 lives.
sum: Operation Blue Star was the Indian army's assault on the Golden Temple at Amritsar in June 1984, to remove armed Sikh militants. It set off the worst year in India since Partition.
